claim: RNA sequencing was performed on a training cohort of 88 RPLS patients.

claim: Cell cycle, DNA damage and repair, and metabolism were identified as the most aberrant biological processes in RPLS.
source: Cell cycle, DNA damage and repair, and metabolism were identified as the most aberrant biological processes in RPLS, enabling the division of RPLS patients into two distinct subtypes with unique molecular signatures, tumor microenvironment, clinical features, and outcomes (overall survival [OS] and disease-free survival [DFS]).
evidence: This finding is based on RNA sequencing data analysis performed in the study.

claim: RPLS patients can be divided into two distinct subtypes with unique molecular signatures, tumor microenvironment, clinical features, and outcomes.

evidence: This is a primary finding based on the RNA sequencing and clustering analysis performed in the study.

claim: A simplified RPLS classification based on LEP and PTTG1 demonstrated high accuracy (AUC>0.99).
source: A simplified RPLS classification based on representative biomarkers (LEP and PTTG1) demonstrated high accuracy (area under the curve [AUC]>0.99), with patients classified as LEP+ and PTTG1-, showing lower aggressive pathological composition ratio and fewer surgery times, along with better OS (HR = 0.41, p<0.001) and DFS (HR = 0.60, p=0.005).
evidence: This is supported by machine learning model performance data presented in the study.

claim: Traditional surgical resection has been regarded as a primary and curable treatment strategy of RPLS for the past 50 years.

claim: The anatomical complexity and biological properties of sarcoma brought great difficulty in achieving microscopically margin-negative resection.
source: However, the anatomical complexity and biological properties of sarcoma brought great difficulty in achieving microscopically margin-negative resection, leading to a high postoperative recurrence rate in RPLS patients.
evidence: This is based on established clinical knowledge about RPLS.

claim: RPLS has a high postoperative recurrence rate.
source: However, the anatomical complexity and biological properties of sarcoma brought great difficulty in achieving microscopically margin-negative resection, leading to a high postoperative recurrence rate in RPLS patients.

claim: Scientists tried to improve the postoperative survival of RPLS patients by personalized surgical resection and neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapies, but the effect was not satisfactory.
source: During the past decade, scientists tried to improve the postoperative survival of RPLS patients by personalized surgical resection and neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapies, but the effect was not satisfactory (Littau et al., 2021; Gronchi et al., 2015; Gronchi et al., 2009; Gronchi and Pollock, 2013; Pisters, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Precision medicine greatly enriched the therapeutic approaches and reformed the clinical decision-making chain of tumor diagnosis and treatment.
source: Recently, precision medicine greatly enriched the therapeutic approaches and reformed the clinical decision-making chain of tumor diagnosis and treatment, prolonging the median survival of main tumor types 2–10 times (Kam et al., 2021; Zeng and Jin, 2022; Alifrangis et al., 2019; Frese et al., 2021).

claim: Precision medicine prolonged the median survival of main tumor types 2–10 times.

claim: The study conducted a comprehensive investigation into the molecular characteristics of RPLS through the largest gene expression landscape ever assembled for this disease.

claim: Two distinct molecular subtypes exist within all RPLS patients, characterized by diverse pathological compositions, enriched signaling pathways, and varying clinical outcomes.

claim: Traditional pathological classification has limitations for surgical decision-making in certain RPLS cases where patients exhibit favorable histological features but poor prognoses.
source: This highlights the limitations of relying solely on traditional pathological classification for surgical decision-making in certain cases where patients exhibit favorable histological features but poor prognoses, emphasizing the pivotal role of molecular subtyping in guiding individualized treatment strategies and enhancing patient management.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that molecular subtypes do not always align with histological features.

claim: Molecular subtyping plays a pivotal role in guiding individualized treatment strategies and enhancing patient management in RPLS.
source: This highlights the limitations of relying solely on traditional pathological classification for surgical decision-making in certain cases where patients exhibit favorable histological features but poor prognoses, emphasizing the pivotal role of molecular subtyping in guiding individualized treatment strategies and enhancing patient management.
